headline: Approved prior meeting minutes; reviewed a deed for 248 Mendon Road and discussed 38 Main Street.
summary: A letter will go to the owners about the deed's wrong address. The meeting then moved into executive session on abatement and exemption applications, as state law requires.
decisions: Approved the open session and executive session minutes of August 18, 2026, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session meeting minutes of August 18, 2026

decision_titles: Open and executive session minutes of August 18, 2026
plain_text:
TOWN OF SUTTON
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
 4 UXBRIDGE ROAD
SUTTON, MA  01590-1702
  508-865-8722
                     Meeting Minutes – August 25, 2026
Present:  Robert Nunnemacher, Chairman
      Matthew Read, Assessor
               Tracey Tardy, Principal Assessor
 
 Meeting called to order at 5:50 p.m.
1.         The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session
            meeting minutes of August 18, 2026
2.         Old & New Business
The Board reviewed a deed for 248 Mendon Road (wrong address listed – will send a letter to the owners to 
advise them).
The Board discussed 38 Main Street prior to the Principal Assessor attending an executive session with the Select 
Board at 5:30pm
3.         Decisions & Actions Taken
4.         Adjourned Open Session @ 5:50 to enter into Executive Session regarding
            Abatements/Exemptions
The Board entered into executive session to review abatement and/or exemption applications pursuant
to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 59, Section 60, and Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7. We are 
meeting in executive session to comply with Chapter 59, Section 60, which limits inspection of Chapter 59 
abatement and exemption applications to assessors and the deputies, clerks and assistants of the assessors, and 
certain other parties listed in the law. Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7 permits public bodies to meet in 
executive session for the purpose of complying with general laws. 
The Board of Assessors adjourned its open meeting at or about 5:50 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted,
Linda Hicks, Assistant Assessor
